analysis.title: If you want a trade after the Sep CPI data, bet that the Dec hike is 50 rather than 25
key_insights: Steve Blitz argues employment follows profits and inflation follows employment. The economy is rounding past the one-year mark of the 2025 low in payroll growth, so base inflation should begin to accelerate.
Acceleration is already visible in rent data, which runs with unemployment, and in service inflation, which follows private payrolls with a lag.
With inflation where it is and the base pace about to accelerate, a funds rate nearing 5% rather than 4% makes more sense.

Unless Warsh is trying to slow the economy with higher term yields, which matter more to private investment than short rates. Blitz doubts Warsh can ignore market credibility concerns because Warsh cares what markets think of him.
Blitz rejects the Administration's late-1990s comparison, in which capital deepening raises real rates and lowers inflation, as a comparison without merit.
The inflation diffusion index shows inflation is broadening but is still not above 50%.

Core CPI and core service inflation excluding rents follow payrolls with a 12-month lag. Given the non-recession recession, the lag may compress to 6 months. Higher base inflation is baked in for the first half of 2027.
Some recent rent weakness is in cities that boomed during COVID and overbuilt. Excess supply is being absorbed and rents are beginning to firm in some of them.

The challenge for Warsh will be how fast he eases once the economy slows, likely kicked off by a poor equity market. Cutting recessions short before disinflation runs its course is one reason the 1970s went the way they did.
Trade view: markets price a 90% chance of a Dec hike. Blitz says pricing should jump to 150% (100% for a 25bp hike plus a 50/50 chance of another 25), so the Dec hike is more likely 50bp than 25bp.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Blitz sees a funds rate near 5% as more consistent with current inflation and accelerating base inflation.
Market pricing is below Blitz's view, which is 150% (100% for a 25bp hike plus a 50/50 chance of another 25bp).
A 50bp hike in Dec is not a zero probability, and pricing should rise to reflect it.
Inflation is broadening but not yet widespread by Blitz's measure.

trade_ideas.description: Bet that the Dec Fed hike is 50bp rather than 25bp (rates trade after the Sep CPI data)
trade_ideas.rationale: Base inflation is set to accelerate as payroll growth passes its 2025 low, and the market prices only a 90% chance of a Dec hike versus Blitz's 150%.
trade_ideas.risk: Warsh may prefer higher term yields to slow the economy rather than larger short-rate hikes, and may care about market credibility.

risk_factors: Warsh may use higher term yields rather than short rates to slow the economy.
A poor equity market could slow the economy and prompt faster easing than the market expects.
The Nov 4 election outcome, which Blitz expects to give Democrats 219 House seats and 51 Senate seats, will shape how lame a duck Trump is.
Policy that cuts recessions short before disinflation runs its course risks a 1970s-style outcome.
geopolitical: Blitz says better inflation would have been the story this year if not for war and tariffs.
